recent_posts.title: AI education strategy, tokenmaxxing, and the synthetic web pollution problem
recent_posts.summary: A newsletter roundup covering several AI and developer topics: the importance of owning developer education in the AI market (featuring Baseten's Philip Kiely), a cautionary tale of an AI agent wiping production data, the 'tokenmaxxing' trend and why maximizing token consumption is a flawed productivity metric, the Talkie LLM trained exclusively on pre-1931 public domain data, a study showing 35% of new websites since 2022 are AI-generated and the risks of model collapse from synthetic data, and a senior engineer's candid career reflections including a take on TDD in the age of agentic coding.

recent_posts.title: The playbook for your agentic SDLC
recent_posts.summary: As agentic AI moves from experimentation to production, engineering leaders need a disciplined framework for operationalizing it within the SDLC. Key principles include establishing business KPIs before deploying agents, measuring performance across the full development lifecycle, and embracing 'bounded autonomy' rather than unchecked agent behavior. Real enterprise deployments succeed through tight orchestration, staged rollouts, human-in-the-loop controls, and continuous instrumentation. The organizations that scale agentic AI effectively are those that prioritize governance, observability, and iterative improvement over raw autonomy.

recent_posts.title: Giving robots a brain | Intrinsic’s Brian Gerkey
recent_posts.summary: A developer newsletter covering several topics: an interview with Intrinsic CTO Brian Gerkey on AI-powered software-defined robotics and ROS; GitHub Copilot's shift to usage-based billing; Anthropic's potential Claude Code pricing changes; 12 agentic harness design patterns distilled from the Claude Code source leak; a Vercel OAuth security breach involving lateral movement through Google Workspace; and the ThoughtWorks Technology Radar's 'lethal trifecta' of agentic AI risk (untrusted content + private data + external communication).

recent_posts.title: How I learned to solve the day two problem for my agents at Salesforce's TDX 2026
recent_posts.summary: A developer-journalist reflects on lessons from Salesforce TDX 2026 about keeping AI agents healthy after initial deployment — the 'day two problem'. Three key insights: Salesforce's Falabella case shows capturing failures and feeding them back into agent instructions creates a self-healing loop; Adobe Population Health's CIO turned compliance audits directly into LLM eval specs at production scale; MuleSoft's SVP argues that existing IT infrastructure (data governance, audit trails, compliance controls) is the enabler — not the blocker — for agentic systems. The post blends conference reporting with personal agent-building experience and ends with a promotional workshop invite.

recent_posts.title: Newsletter roundup on AI coding agents, small models, and developer productivity
recent_posts.summary: A newsletter roundup covering AI coding and productivity topics: Ai2's Tim Dettmers explains how his team built the SERA model with minimal compute by synthesizing training data from private codebases; Andrej Karpathy's agentic Zettelkasten approach to self-maintaining knowledge bases; the 'Water Town' agent swarm data stack for data teams; Google Gemma 4 running offline on iPhone; why using Obsidian flat files as AI memory doesn't scale; managing mental fatigue from multi-agent workflows; and Google's new spam policy against back-button hijacking.

recent_posts.title: Lessons from infrastructure leaders on taking AI from prototype to production
recent_posts.summary: Reflections from a panel at HumanX 2026 featuring infrastructure leaders from Guidewheel, Anyscale, and Thread AI on what it actually takes to move AI from demo to production. Key themes: layer AI on top of existing systems rather than replacing them, invest heavily in observability before you need it, rethink human-in-the-loop as a callable resource rather than a gatekeeper, and measure business outcomes (P&L, team velocity, cost) rather than adoption metrics. The consensus: taking AI to production is as much an organizational challenge as a technical one, and the gap between a working demo and a reliable production system is where most AI projects fail.

recent_posts.title: LLMs are a technological leap without a ramp
recent_posts.summary: A personal reflection on how LLM adoption differs from previous tech shifts like git or Docker — it happened without a conscious decision. The author argues that unlike past paradigm changes, AI tools compressed the adaptation window so fast that many developers didn't notice the transition. The core message is blunt: developers who deliberately choose to sit out AI adoption aren't just missing a skill, they're opting out of what software engineering is becoming, and that choice will have serious career consequences. The window to start is still open, but it's closing.

recent_posts.title: The guardian in the machine | Wayfound’s Tatyana Mamut
recent_posts.summary: A newsletter covering several AI topics: Wayfound CEO Tatyana Mamut discusses why traditional software testing fails for stochastic AI models and the need for independent guardian agents. Anthropic's Claude Mythos model is highlighted for its security implications, alongside Anthropic's Project Glasswing — a $100M initiative with the Linux Foundation to secure critical software infrastructure. Additional items cover how to read AI model benchmarks (with ARC-AGI-3 as a new standard), four new open-source frontier models (Gemma 4, Bonsai, Trinity, Holo3) under Apache 2.0 licenses, and a Claude plugin called Caveman that compresses AI outputs to reduce token costs by up to 87%.

recent_posts.title: Stop measuring AI adoption. Start measuring AI impact. | LinearB’s APEX framework
recent_posts.summary: A newsletter covering several AI and engineering topics: LinearB's APEX framework for measuring AI impact on software delivery (beyond DORA/SPACE), GitHub Copilot's controversial PR advertisement incident, Anthropic's accidental leak of Claude Code's source revealing zero tests and a 3000-line function, Shopify's 75x inference cost reduction using fine-tuned Qwen 3 models, managing open source projects flooded with AI-generated PRs, and a new JavaScript library called Pretext that bypasses CSS for text rendering.

recent_posts.title: Why AI-assisted PRs merge at half the rate of human code | LinearB’s 2026 Benchmarks
recent_posts.summary: LinearB's 2026 Engineering Benchmarks reveal that AI-assisted pull requests merge at less than half the rate of human-authored code, despite 88%+ developer AI adoption. The core issue: AI accelerates code generation but exposes bottlenecks in review processes and unclear requirements. The newsletter also covers MCP's evolving relevance, context anchoring to combat AI memory loss in long sessions, how AI amplifies existing workflow bottlenecks rather than solving them, and emerging workplace etiquette issues around sharing unverified AI output.

top_posts.title: The 11 Types Of Toxic Pull Requests (According To 4.5 Million Code Branches)
